summary: Secukinumab (Cosentyx) is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody that selectively targets interleukin-17A (IL-17A), used for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, enthesitis-related arthritis, and hidradenitis suppurativa, with both subcutaneous and intravenous (PsA/AS/nr-axSpA) formulations. Typical dosing loads at Weeks 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 then continues every 4 weeks - 300 mg for plaque psoriasis and HS, 150 mg for the spondyloarthritis/PsA indications (escalating to 300 mg if needed). It has no boxed warning but increases the risk of serious infections, so patients must be evaluated for active or latent tuberculosis before initiation. Notable cautions include new-onset or exacerbation of inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis), serious hypersensitivity reactions (anaphylaxis, angioedema, urticaria), and severe eczematous eruptions. Live vaccines should be avoided during therapy.

admin: Evaluate for active or latent tuberculosis and complete all age-appropriate vaccinations before the first dose
300 mg subcutaneous doses are administered as two 150 mg injections; available as prefilled syringe, Sensoready pen, and 300 mg/2 mL UnoReady pen
Bring the prefilled syringe/pen to room temperature before injecting; do not shake (avoid foaming); inspect for particulates/discoloration
Inject subcutaneously into the abdomen, thigh, or upper outer arm; rotate injection sites and avoid tender, bruised, or affected skin
Intravenous formulation (PsA/AS/nr-axSpA) must be diluted prior to use and infused over 30 minutes by a healthcare professional
Avoid live vaccines during treatment; patients may self-inject after appropriate training; the removable cap of certain devices contains natural rubber latex
moa: Secukinumab is a recombinant high-affinity human IgG1/kappa monoclonal antibody that selectively binds to the proinflammatory cytokine interleukin-17A (IL-17A) and inhibits its interaction with the IL-17 receptor. IL-17A is a naturally occurring cytokine central to normal inflammatory and immune responses and is overexpressed in psoriatic skin and inflamed joints. By neutralizing IL-17A, secukinumab inhibits the downstream release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines and the recruitment of neutrophils, thereby reducing the inflammation that drives plaque psoriasis, spondyloarthritis, and related conditions. As a human IgG1 antibody it is degraded into peptides and amino acids via catabolic pathways like endogenous IgG.

preg: Limited human data are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk of adverse developmental outcomes. In an embryo-fetal development study in cynomolgus monkeys, no malformations or embryo-fetal toxicity occurred at subcutaneous doses up to 30 times the maximum recommended human dose during organogenesis. As an IgG antibody, transplacental transfer increases in the third trimester. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed; the U.S. background risk of major birth defects is 2-4% and of miscarriage 15-20%.
lact: It is not known whether secukinumab is excreted in human milk or absorbed systemically after ingestion, and there are no data on effects on the breastfed child or on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the infant.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment; secukinumab is a monoclonal antibody and is not eliminated by the kidneys. No dedicated renal-impairment studies have been conducted.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is provided for hepatic impairment, and no dedicated hepatic studies have been performed. Secukinumab is not recommended in patients with active viral hepatitis; monitor for hepatitis B virus reactivation, which has been reported.

major: Live vaccines - avoid during therapy (immunosuppression; risk of vaccine-associated infection)
moderate: Certain CYP450 substrates with a narrow therapeutic index (e.g., warfarin, cyclosporine) - resolution of chronic inflammation on starting (or relapse on stopping) secukinumab can normalize CYP enzyme formation and alter substrate levels; monitor effect/concentration and adjust as needed
Other immunosuppressants/biologics - additive infection risk (combinations not adequately studied)

counsel: This medicine lowers your immune defenses - call your doctor at the first sign of infection (fever, cough, persistent sore, night sweats, burning with urination)
You will be tested for TB before starting; tell your doctor if you have had TB or been near someone with TB
Tell your doctor if you have Crohn disease or ulcerative colitis, or develop new or worsening stomach pain, cramps, diarrhea, or blood in the stool
Get emergency help for trouble breathing, throat tightness, swelling of the face/lips/tongue, or a severe rash or hives (signs of a serious allergic reaction)
Do not receive live vaccines while on treatment; let your doctor know the cap of some pens/syringes contains latex if you have a latex allergy
Learn proper subcutaneous injection technique and site rotation; store in the refrigerator and let it reach room temperature before injecting - do not shake
pk: Clinical improvement typically develops over the first weeks of therapy; steady state by approximately Week 24 on every-4-week dosing
Subcutaneous Cmax reached by approximately 6 days (Tmax); 27.3 mcg/mL after a single 300 mg dose, 13.7 mcg/mL after 150 mg
Every-4-week maintenance dosing sustains therapeutic trough concentrations (bioavailability ~55-77%)

Refrigerate at 2-8 C (36-46 F) in original carton to protect from light; do not freeze; do not shake; if removed from refrigeration may be kept up to 4 days at room temperature not exceeding 30 C (86 F)
pearls: Carries a risk of SERIOUS INFECTION - evaluate for active or latent tuberculosis BEFORE initiation, treat latent TB first, and monitor for infection throughout; serious bacterial, viral, and fungal opportunistic (including some fatal) infections have been reported with IL-17 inhibitors
May cause new onset or EXACERBATION of INFLAMMATORY BOWEL DISEASE (Crohn disease / ulcerative colitis) - use caution and counsel patients to report new or worsening GI symptoms
No boxed warning (unlike TNF inhibitors), but serious hypersensitivity (anaphylaxis, angioedema) and severe eczematous eruptions can occur
Loading schedule is Weeks 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 then every 4 weeks; 300 mg for plaque psoriasis and HS, 150 mg (escalate to 300 mg if needed) for PsA/AS/nr-axSpA

Avoid live vaccines and complete age-appropriate immunizations before starting; monitor for hepatitis B reactivation and do not use in active viral hepatitis; the device cap of some products contains natural rubber latex
missed: If a dose is missed, administer it as soon as remembered, then resume the regular dosing schedule (do not double up). For significant delays during the weekly loading phase or maintenance, contact the prescriber for guidance on resuming the schedule.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Doses up to 30 mg/kg intravenously have been administered in clinical trials without dose-limiting toxicity. In the event of overdose, monitor the patient for any signs or symptoms of adverse reactions and institute appropriate symptomatic treatment; consider contacting the Poison Help line (1-800-222-1222) or a medical toxicologist.
